title: Policies cleared in fatality review
article: The Calgary Police Service's own review of a deadly shooting last year has upheld a fatality inquiry into the incident.

The review into the police service's staffing and dispatch policies for top-priority calls was recommended by provincial court Judge Heather Lamoureux, who presided over a fatality inquiry into the death of 34-year-old Arthur George Provencal last year.

"We conducted this thorough review and, as a result of the review, we've determined that our policy is not only consistent with most other police agencies in Canada and the U.S., but that it adequately addresses the issue of officer safety, community safety and balancing the workload of officers in the field," said Calgary police Deputy Chief Rick Hanson.
On Dec. 23, 2000, Const. Julien Gagne was sent alone to the scene of an armed robbery that turned into a hostage-taking.

Provencal, who was on parole at the time of the incident, was shot between the eyes by Gagne as he held a knife to the throat of an employee during a bungled robbery at Shoppers Drug Mart in TD Square.

During the inquiry, Lamoureux said she believed Gagne did the right thing by shooting Provencal as he pressed the 30-centimetre blade against Ernie Plaxton, an employee who put himself between the agitated man and three frightened co-workers.

But Lamoureux also said that although there is no way of knowing if two officers could have defused the situation, Calgary police should examine the ability of one officer versus teams of two officers.
This week, the Calgary police completed its review supporting its use of one-officer police cars and submitted it to the province's attorney general.
Hanson said 84 per cent of all the service's 250,000 annual calls require only one officer.
